title: Layers, Levers, and the Map of Taxonomies
subtitle: The five layers every receipt itemizes, and the four strategy families that shrink them
topics: The five context layers: system, retrieved, tool, history, user — the receipt's unit of account
The four canonical strategies: write, select, compress, isolate [LC-WSCI]
Which layer each of the app's ten modes attacks, read straight off the receipts
The taxonomy map: translating add/compress/retrieve/offload and crop/compress/summarize/select into the canonical frame
Two levers that don't fit the families: caching (position economics) and routing (choosing levers)

analogy.title: Four Ways to Lighten a Suitcase
analogy.text: Every overweight suitcase has the same four remedies. You can ship things ahead to the hotel so they never ride in the bag (write — external memory). You can pack only what this trip needs instead of your whole wardrobe (select). You can vacuum-bag what you do pack (compress). Or you can hand half the load to a travel companion with their own bag who meets you there (isolate). Buying airline status so bags fly cheaper changes none of the packing — that's caching, an economics move. And the seasoned traveler's real skill is knowing which remedy fits which trip — that's routing.

antiPatterns: Strategy-as-incantation: turning on 'compression' everywhere because a blog said 70% savings — without knowing which layer it attacks, you compress the one layer that was already small
Taxonomy fights: teams argue whether something is 'retrieval' or 'offloading' instead of asking which layer shrinks and what the receipt says — the map exists so the words stop mattering

Ignoring the two misfits: treating caching as a token reduction (it isn't — same tokens, cheaper reads) or treating routing as a fifth lever (it chooses levers; it is only as good as the graded evidence behind it)

sections.title: 🔬 On the bench
sections.body:
Do: Pin preset Q9 and ask it in every one of the ten toggles, left to right.

See: Watch the receipt's shape change per mode — and note which single toggle changes the verdict: compressed stamps ✕ FAILED on Q9. That stamp is the course's law.

Bench not running? App guide · SETUP.md

sections.title: Five Layers: the Receipt's Unit of Account
sections.body:
Every TokenReceipt in MedFlow itemizes input across five layers. System: the standing instructions and persona — identical on every call unless you change the design. Retrieved: whatever the assembler pulled from the domain — in naive mode, essentially the whole seeded database as JSON. Tool: results of lookups the model (or a sub-agent) performed mid-call. History: the conversation so far. User: the question itself — routinely the smallest line on the bill.

Read one real bill. Naive mode on Q9 ("summarize member M-2001's history") bills 1,700 input tokens; the retrieved layer dominates because naive ships every member, every request, every criterion — including all three procedures' criteria tables that have nothing to do with Rosa Delgado. The question needed two requests: PA-1001 (APPROVED) and PA-1004 (MANUAL_REVIEW). Everything else was paid-for noise. Diagnosis always starts here: which layer dominates, and did the answer need it?

sections.title: Four Families, Ten Modes
sections.body:
LangChain's canonical frame names four strategy families ([LC-WSCI]): Write — persist context outside the window and read back only what's needed (the app's notes mode: structured notes replace raw history; Q9 for 167 tokens). Select — pull in only what helps (the jit, graph, and okf modes: identifiers-then-lookup, a provenance-tagged subgraph, or one canonical concept file; Q3 via okf costs 186 tokens against naive's 1,696 — a 9.1x cut on the same graded answer). Compress — retain only required tokens (budgeted caps and evicts whole records; compressed runs prune → extract-verbatim → abstract with a fidelity assertion). Isolate — give the messy work a clean window (isolated: a sub-call gathers, the main call gets its ≤1.5K summary).

Two toggles refuse the families. Cached reorders context static-first and marks the prefix cacheable — the same 731 tokens, but most become cheap cache reads on repeat calls: position economics, not reduction. Routed picks one of the others per question class — a meta-lever whose entire authority comes from graded measurements (U12's subject).

One honest wrinkle from the grid: isolated bills MORE than naive on single questions (1,805 median vs 1,696) because the sub-call's own tokens land in the tool layer, visibly. Isolation buys clean attention and pays in total tokens; it wins on long sessions and parallel research, not one-shot asks [ANTHROPIC-CE]. The receipt refuses to hide that trade — that's the point of receipts. (All numbers: replay grid, synthetic-pre-recording labels.)

sections.title: The Map of Taxonomies
sections.body: You will meet other vocabularies in the wild, including in this course's own parents. The agent-course M03B teaches add / compress / retrieve / offload; the kit's open-source track uses crop / compress / summarize / select. The map: retrieve ≈ select; offload splits — offloading to files/memory is write, offloading to sub-agents is isolate; add is the decision the other levers discipline (what deserves inclusion at all); crop and summarize are both compress (drop vs distill). When vocabularies clash, stop arguing names and point at the receipt: which layer shrank, and did the stamp stay green? The layer-and-verdict view is the taxonomy-independent truth. Both parent courses go deeper: the kit for each lever's craft (context-eng-kit), the graph course for select-by-structure (knowledge-graph).

sections.question: Q9's naive receipt shows retrieved at ~1,400 of 1,700 tokens. A teammate proposes 'better summarization of the conversation history.' WHY is that the wrong first move?
options: A. Summarization is always lossy, so it should never be used
B. History isn't the dominant layer — compressing a small layer can't fix a bill dominated by retrieved; the first move is a select-family lever aimed at what's actually big
C. The history layer can't be compressed in this app
D. Because caching would be free
sections.explanation: Diagnosis before strategy: the receipt says retrieved dominates, so select (jit/graph/okf) attacks the actual problem. Aiming compress at the wrong layer is the strategy-as-incantation anti-pattern.

sections.question: WHEN does the isolated mode's higher single-call bill (1,805 vs naive's 1,696) become a good trade?
options: B. When the question is tiny
C. On long or parallel workloads, where sub-agents keep the main window clean and hand back condensed summaries — the per-call premium buys attention that compounds across a session
D. Whenever caching is also enabled
sections.explanation: Task-context alignment [ANTHROPIC-CE]: isolation's price is visible per-call in the tool layer, and its payoff is session-scale focus. One-shot questions pay the premium without collecting the benefit.

sections.question: Your team's compressed mode cut Q9 to 208 tokens — an 88% saving — and the stamp reads ✗ FAILED (PA-1004 missing). What is the correct report to leadership?
options: A. '88% token reduction achieved on aggregation queries'
B. 'Compression works but grading is too strict'
C. 'No saving on Q9: the compressed arm dropped a load-bearing fact, so its number is void; budgeted (565, PASS) is the current honest best for that class'
D. 'We should average the PASS and FAIL runs'
sections.explanation: Savings void is not a slogan, it's the reporting rule. The honest comparison is among correct arms only — and the fix (a fidelity assertion that refuses to drop identifiers) is U07's subject.

sections.title: What Goes Wrong
items: Lever monoculture: one strategy applied to all ten question classes — the grid shows no mode wins everywhere (okf wins canonical at 186, notes wins aggregation at 167, isolated loses every single-shot)
Vocabulary lock-in: a team standardizes on one taxonomy and then can't absorb techniques described in another — the map costs one slide and ends the problem
Compressing the user layer: shaving the 19-token question while a 1,400-token retrieved dump rides along untouched

takeaway: Diagnose by layer, act by family: name the dominant line on the receipt, pick the strategy family that attacks it, and let the stamp — not the taxonomy — decide if it worked.
labUnderstand: Ask the same standing question (Q9) in all ten modes, classify every mode into write/select/compress/isolate from its receipt shape, and watch the Compare drawer void an 88% saving when compressed drops PA-1004.
labBuild: Have Claude write layer_profile.py — a script that asks one question across all ten modes, prints a layer-by-mode matrix, and names the dominant layer and the family that should attack it for each mode.
